before.title: Marrakech – Toubkal Refuge
body: The trek departs from Marrakech around 9:00 AM (seasonal variations apply) for an exhilarating 1.5-hour transfer south through the dramatic Mly Brahim gorges to the Berber town of Imlil (1,740 m ). Nestled in the upper foothills of the Western High Atlas Mountains, Imlil is a major trailhead, with mule paths branching off in all directions.

From Imlil, we trek approximately 8 km to the picturesque village of Sidi Chamharouch, set beside a waterfall and stream. The village’s pisé homes appear built one into another, creating a charming and unique atmosphere. Sidi Chamharouch is a place of pilgrimage for devout Muslims, home to a marabout shrine —a sacred site not accessible to non-Muslims and believed to originate from pre-Islamic religious traditions.

We pause for a field picnic with full views of the mighty Jbel Toubkal (4,167 m ), the highest peak in the Maghreb. After lunch, the trek continues up to the Toubkal Refuge, where dinner is served and you stay overnight in the refuge’s dormitory-style accommodation .

before.title: Mount Toubkal
body: We begin early with breakfast before setting out around 6:00 AM for the climb to Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m ), the highest peak in the Maghreb. The climb is non-technical but steep, taking approximately 3 hours, and offers breathtaking panoramic views—the highlight of your trek.

The first recorded ascent of Toubkal was made in 1923 by French mountaineers V. Berger, M. Doubleau, and the Marquis de Segonzac, and the mountain has since attracted countless trekkers seeking this highly rewarding experience.

After enjoying the summit views, we descend via the Ikkhibi Sud / South Cirque , a straightforward route with your guide, taking 2–3 hours back toward the Toubkal Refuge . Here, we enjoy a picnic lunch , followed by a gentle hike down in the afternoon.
The day concludes with dinner and overnight accommodation at the refuge, giving you a chance to rest and reflect on your remarkable achievement.

before.title: Toubkal Refuge – Marrakech
body: After breakfast , we set off north along steep, zigzagging trails descending from the higher slopes of the Assif n’Isougan n’Ouagounss Valley toward the Berber village of Sidi Chamharouch (3,106 m ).

Before entering the village, your guide will show you a sacred tree , adorned with colored cloth strips and stones—a traditional site of significance for the local Berber communities. After a brief stop to relax, particularly welcome on a warm day, we continue the descent high above the Assif Aït Mizane Valley, winding down granite and basalt grey rocks for approximately 8 km to reach the fertile Berber village of Aroumd (Aremd, 1,840 m ), surrounded by terraced fields of maize, onions, and fruit trees.

We pause for a picnic lunch , before taking a well-defined mule track that zigzags along the valley floor for 4 km, arriving at Imlil around 1–2 PM. Here, enjoy a welcome glass of traditional mint tea at the home of our senior guide. Following this, we transfer back to Marrakech , arriving around 4 PM and concluding your unforgettable trek through the High Atlas Mountains.

before.title: Marrakech → Agersioual → Matat → Tizi Oudid → Ouaougmout
body: - Transport: ~1.5 hrs
- Hiking distance: ~10 km | 4–5 hrs
- Elevation gain/loss: 1,600 m → 2,219 m → 1,730 m
- Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner
- Accommodation: Berber Guest House, Ouaougmout
- Guide & mule support included
Itinerary:

Depart from Marrakech for a scenic drive south through the Tahnaoute and Moulay Brahim gorges, passing the town of Asni, famous for its weekly Berber market on Saturdays. Continue to Agersioual (1,600m), where you’ll meet your Berber muleteer crew—always a fun and lively start to the trek.

The hike begins in a north-westerly direction, following traditional mule tracks up cornfields and juniper woods toward the Tizi Oudid Pass (2,219m). Pause here to take in sweeping views of the Imlil and n’Aït Ouissadene Valleys.

Continue for another 30 minutes to Id Issa, where a picnic lunch is served amidst high peaks and surrounding valleys. After lunch, descend for approximately 1.5 hours along a dirt track to the Assif n’Aït Ouissadene River and the red clay village of Ouaougmout (1,730m).
Dinner and overnight stay will be at a traditional Berber guest house, offering an authentic experience of local hospitality.

before.title: Tiziane → Azzaden Valley → Tizi Oussem → Azib Tamsoult
body: - Hiking distance: ~12 km | 4–5 hrs
- Elevation gain/loss: ~1,900 m → 2,250 m → 2,250 m
- Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner
- Accommodation: Refuge Tamsoult (Dormitory)
- Guide & mule support included
Itinerary:

After a hearty breakfast at Tiziane, your local mountain guide and muleteer will accompany you on a spectacular hike through the Azzaden Valley, known locally as the “Valley of Colors” for its vibrant orchards and terraced fields.

The trail climbs gently along the northern slopes of Mt Toubkal, offering panoramic views of the High Atlas peaks as you move through Tizi Oussem, a small village where you may see local shepherds and their flocks grazing.

Next, you’ll reach Azib Tamsoult (2,250m) via the Irhouliden cascade waterfalls, a refreshing stop where the sound of rushing water and misty air adds to the magical mountain atmosphere. Here, you’ll enjoy a picnic lunch above the waterfalls, taking in the fresh alpine air and dramatic views of the surrounding peaks and valleys.

After lunch, the trail continues for a short descent back to Azib Tamsoult Refuge, where you’ll settle into the dormitory accommodation. The refuge is perched perfectly for sunset views over the Azzaden Valley, and the evening offers time to relax, chat with fellow trekkers, and enjoy a hearty traditional Berber dinner.
This day combines nature, culture, and mountain adventure, giving trekkers an authentic experience of High Atlas life and landscapes.
Overnight at Refuge Tamsoult

before.title: Azzadene Valley → Tizi n’Mzik Pass → Azib Brdoun → Imlil
before.accommodation: Return to Marrakech or optional Imlil Village Guesthouse
body: - Transport: ~1.5 hrs
- Hiking distance: ~12 km | 4–5 hrs
- Elevation gain/loss: 1,850 m → 2,479 m → 1,980 m
- Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch
- Accommodation: Optional: Armed Village Guesthouse (extra cost) or return to Marrakech
- Guide & mule support included
Itinerary:

After breakfast at your accommodation in Azib Tamsoult / Imlil, your guide and muleteer will lead you on a fantastic climb out of the Azzadene Valley. The trail ascends steadily toward the Tizi n’Mzik Pass (2,479 m), offering dramatic panoramic views of the High Atlas peaks and valleys below—a perfect spot for photos and short rest stops.

From the pass, begin a gentle descent toward Azib Brdoun (1,850 m), where your picnic lunch awaits amid the tranquil mountain scenery. After lunch, continue through the Armed Village area, enjoying the local architecture, terraced fields, and the serene sound of nearby streams and Imlil waterfalls.
From here, guests have two options:
- Return to Marrakech in the late afternoon (included).
- Optional overnight at Imlil Village “Riad Berber Towers” (extra cost) at 1,980 m, located on the foothills of Toubkal, offering a truly authentic mountain experience before descending the next day.
This day combines challenging hiking, stunning mountain views, and cultural insights into Berber life in the High Atlas.

before.title: Marrakech → Moulay Brahim Gorges → Asni → Imi Oughlad → Gliz
body: Your adventure begins with a morning transfer from bustling Marrakech (450 m) into the foothills of the Atlas. You’ll drive through the winding Moulay Brahim Gorges and the lively town of Asni (1,150 m), famous for its weekly Saturday Berber market.

On arrival at Imi Oughlad (1,450 m), you’ll meet your local muleteer crew and set off on your first hike. The trail climbs steadily through pine, juniper, and terraced farmlands to Tizi N’Elbour Pass (1,700 m). From here, enjoy sweeping views of the valleys below. Continue through tiny hamlets like Imsker and Tinghar, before descending gently to Gliz village (1,650 m).
Picnic lunch en route under walnut or pine trees.
Dinner with a Berber family offers your first taste of Atlas hospitality.
Hiking: 4–5 hrs | Ascent: +500 m | Descent: -250 m
Overnight in a Berber family house in Gliz.

before.title: Gliz → Amssakrou → Tizi N’Ougrssioual → Matat
body: Today’s trek takes you through some of the most beautiful farmlands in the region. Walk along walnut groves and terraced fields in Amssakrou Valley, following shepherd paths that link remote villages.
Picnic lunch along the trail near riverside fields.
The highlight is the climb to Tizi N’Ougrssioual Pass (2,000 m), where the red clay villages of the Azzaden Valley come into view against the backdrop of snow-capped peaks.
After descending into the valley, stop for lunch near Agrssioual village before continuing to Matat (1,800 m).
Dinner in a guest house, with hearty tagine and fresh bread baked in a clay oven.
Hiking: 5–6 hrs | Ascent: +400 m | Descent: -500 m
Overnight in a Berber guest house in Matat.

before.title: Matat → Tizi Oudid → Id Issa → Tizi Oussem → Azib Tamsoult
body: After breakfast, climb gradually towards Tizi Oudid Pass (2,200 m), a balcony with magnificent views of the High Atlas. Descend through juniper forests and traditional Berber hamlets to reach Id Issa village.

Continue deeper into the Azzaden Valley, known for its dramatic red-earth landscapes and walnut groves. Pass through Tizi Oussem (1,850 m), one of the valley’s largest villages, before reaching Azib Tamsoult (2,250 m),Lunch with views of terraced walnut groves. a summer pasture hamlet where shepherds graze their flocks.
Enjoy a hot meal in the evening surrounded by high peaks.
Hiking: 6 hrs | Ascent: +700 m | Descent: -400 m
Overnight in Refuge Tamsoult (2,250 m).

before.title: Azib Tamsoult → Ighouliden Waterfalls → Tizi Mzik → Imlil
body: A spectacular day! Begin with a short hike to the Ighouliden waterfalls (2,400 m), cascading down rocky cliffs – one of the most beautiful spots in the Atlas. From here, climb steadily to Tizi Mzik Pass (2,489 m), Picnic lunch at the pass or during descent. offering panoramic views of the Azzaden and Imlil valleys.
Descend on mule tracks lined with juniper and wildflowers until you reach Imlil (1,750 m), the main trailhead village of the High Atlas.
A traditional dinner awaits you at Riad Berber Towers, with warm Berber hospitality.
Hiking: 6–7 hrs | Ascent: +600 m | Descent: -950 m
Overnight at Riad Berber Towers, Imlil.

before.title: Imlil → Sidi Chamharouch → Imlil
body: Today’s hike leads you towards the holy site of Sidi Chamharouch (2,350 m), Picnic lunch near the shrine by the river. known for its white-painted shrine dedicated to the “King of the Devils.” Pilgrims come here seeking blessings and healing. The trail climbs steadily along the Mizane Valley, passing streams, walnut groves, and views of Mount Toubkal (4,167 m).
Have a picnic lunch by the river before descending back to Imlil.
Hiking: 4–5 hrs | Ascent: +600 m | Descent: -600 m
Overnight at Riad Berber Towers, Imlil.

before.title: Imlil → Short Hike with Lunch→ Marrakech
body: After breakfast, enjoy a gentle hike around Imlil’s surrounding villages – Aremd, Tamatert, or Mzik – to see traditional stone houses, terraced fields, and local life.
Lunch with a Berber family, tasting freshly baked bread, olive oil, and homegrown vegetables.
Afternoon transfer back to Marrakech (~1.5 hrs).
Arrival in the early evening, with memories of valleys, villages, and waterfalls.
Hiking: 2–3 hrs | Easy walk

before.title: AGOUTI – AZIB AROUS

body: Trek up through wide grazing pastures to cross the Aghouri pass at 3,450m with superb views of the plateau below and the Mgoun Ridge. Descend to the wind-eroded and snow-covered high plateau of Tarkedit (2,900m) overnight in camp. Approx. 6 hrs walking

After following the ridge for a further 2km past the summit, we descend into the Oulilimt Valley and camp overnight near the Oulilimt water spring, Approx. 9 hrs walking

body: Upon arrival at Casablanca airport, you’ll be welcomed by your driver/guide. If time allows, begin with a visit to the majestic Hassan II Mosque, perched dramatically on the Atlantic and one of the largest mosques in the world. Its intricate mosaics, marble columns, and soaring minaret set the tone for Morocco’s architectural wonders.

From there, you’ll journey south through rolling plains toward Marrakech, the “Red City,” known for its bustling souks and rich history. After check-in at your riad, enjoy your first evening wandering the magical Jemaa el-Fna Square, alive with musicians, storytellers, and food stalls.
Meals: X

before.title: Guided Visit of Marrakech
body: A full day dedicated to exploring Marrakech with a licensed city guide. Start at the Koutoubia Mosque, an iconic landmark visible across the city, before stepping inside the lavishly decorated Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece. Visit the Saadian Tombs, where intricate stucco and marble reflect Moorish craftsmanship.

In the afternoon, dive into the labyrinth of the souks, where vibrant stalls overflow with spices, textiles, leather, and lanterns. End the day in the Jemaa el-Fna, which transforms into a nightly open-air theater of Moroccan life.
Meals: Breakfast

before.title: Free Day in Marrakech
body: Today you leave from El Jadida, you will reach El Oualidia, the pearl of the Atlantic Ocean, this town is a stunningly picturesque little resort – a fishing port and lagoon beach, flanked by a kasbah and a royal villa. The kasbah is seventeenth century, built by the Saadian Sultan El Oualid (after whom the village is named) as a counterweight and alternative to El Jadida, then held by the Portuguese. Until Sultan Sidi Mohammed took El Jadida, the extensive lagoon made an excellent harbour and, as late as 1875, a French geographer thought that “by a little dredging the place would again become the safest shipping station on the whole Moroccan seaboard”. The royal villa, which now stands empty, was built by Mohammed V, who celebrated many birthdays and other family events here. Your afternoon will be devoted to enjoy the beach; a sea food lunch is available to be served at the beach. Your day will end accommodations at the Hotel/raid.
Meals: Breakfast

before.title: Marrakech – Agafay Desert
body: Leave the city behind and head into the Agafay Desert, a dramatic stony landscape stretching to the foothills of the Atlas. Upon arrival, you’ll settle into a luxury camp with sweeping views. Spend the afternoon on a camel trek or try quad biking across the rocky plateaus.
As the sun sets, watch the desert turn golden before enjoying a candlelit dinner under the stars, accompanied by Berber hospitality and music. Overnight in comfortable tents with modern amenities.
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner

body: Today you’ll climb into the High Atlas Mountains, Morocco’s most scenic range. Stop for a warm Berber family lunch in a traditional home, where you’ll learn about rural mountain life. Later, enjoy a gentle hike around Imlil, walking through terraced fields, walnut groves, and small villages at the foot of Mount Toubkal.
Overnight in a cozy mountain guesthouse or boutique lodge, surrounded by the serenity of the peaks.

before.title: Marrakech – Toubkal National Park – Marrakech
body: Escape the bustle of Marrakech and immerse yourself in the majestic scenery of the High Atlas Mountains on this full-day adventure to Toubkal National Park, home to North Africa’s highest peak. This trip offers a perfect combination of nature, culture, and local tradition.
Journey to Imlil

Your day begins with pickup from your hotel or riad in Marrakech at 09:00 AM. Travel in a private vehicle through the winding roads of the Atlas foothills, enjoying scenic mountain views, valleys, and traditional Berber villages along the way. Upon arrival in Imlil, meet your experienced local mountain guide who will lead you through the park.
Hike through Toubkal Valley

The hike begins in the lush Toubkal Valley, passing through green fields adorned with apple, walnut, and cherry trees. As you ascend, the views of Adj Mountain (3,100 m), Aglzim Mountain (3,900 m), and Mount Toubkal (4,167 m) dominate the landscape. The route combines gentle pathways with moderate inclines, offering opportunities to observe traditional mountain life, terraced farms, and local wildlife.
Sidi Chamarouch Shrine

Along the trail, reach Sidi Chamarouch (2,315 m), a small village and holy shrine dedicated to a revered local saint. Pilgrims have visited this site for centuries, and it remains a spiritual and cultural landmark. While non-Muslim visitors cannot cross the bridge into the shrine, you can admire its unique architecture and take photos from outside.
Picnic Lunch

Enjoy a traditional picnic lunch by the river and a waterfall, served on Berber carpets. Your chef prepares fresh Moroccan dishes, allowing you to savor the flavors of the Atlas while surrounded by breathtaking natural scenery. Take your time to relax, explore the area, and capture the tranquil beauty of the surroundings.
Return to Marrakech

After lunch, descend back to Armed Village, enjoying the stunning valley views along the way. Return to Marrakech by private transport in the afternoon, concluding a day filled with adventure, culture, and unforgettable mountain landscapes.

body: Essaouira Day Trip – Coastal City, Medina & Argan Experience
Includes: Private transport (approx. 2.5 hours each way), professional guide, and optional activities.

Start your day with breakfast in Marrakech, then depart for Essaouira, a charming seaside town with a rich cultural and historical heritage. The journey passes through scenic landscapes, small roadside towns, and occasional Berber villages.

Essaouira, formerly known as Mogador, has long been a cultural hub, attracting famous musicians like Jimi Hendrix, Bob Marley, and Cat Stevens in the 1960s and 70s. Visit this UNESCO World Heritage-listed medina, featuring white-washed buildings with blue shutters, thuya wood workshops, art galleries, and a variety of seafood restaurants.
Tour Highlights:
- Explore the medina, including the spice and jewelry souks
- Visit Place Prince Moulay El Hassan and the Skala du Port for breathtaking views of the Portuguese ramparts and fishing harbor
- Stop at an Argan Cooperative to see how women produce argan oil, nut butter, and cosmetics
- Optional winery visit for wine and cheese tasting in the Essaouira region
- Lunch at a traditional fish-grill café overlooking the Atlantic Ocean
- Visit Orson Welles’ Square, commemorating the filming of Othello in Essaouira

For adventure enthusiasts, consider side excursions at Ranch de Diabat, offering quad biking, camel or horse rides, and water sports such as kayaking, windsurfing, or surfing (weather permitting). Essaouira is famously known as the wind capital of Africa, making it ideal for water sports enthusiasts.
Return to Marrakech in the late afternoon, completing a day filled with culture, history, and coastal beauty.

before.title: Marrakesh – Essaouira
body: Departure at 9 o’clock in the morning when the driver will come to fetch you from whichever riad or hotel you might be staying in. You will take the motor-way, passing thousands of Morocco-specific argane trees on the way to this blue and white, very individual, sea-side town and port. Essaouira is many tourists’ darling! Previously known as Mogador to the Portuguese inhabitants, it is a charming place, well- known for local handicrafts, especially thuja wood furniture, carving and small artefacts, sold in innumerable shops along the windy streets. At the sea front, the customer chooses a selection of freshly caught fish to have prepared on the spot. Essaouira has a favourable micro-climate; mild in winter and cool in summer, although frequently windy, which makes it very popular among surfers.

before.title: Essaouira – Sidi Ifni
body: Leaving Essaouira after breakfast, you follow the coastal road south with constant views of the Atlantic, often battering the rocks and sending up picturesque spray as it beats against the rocks. We pass Agadir and continue south to Tiznit, the town famous for its silver jewelry. From here we turn towards the sea and take the particularly beautiful coastal road to Sid Ifni. This is a little neat blue and white town with a distinctly Spanish feel to it. It takes its name from a local holy man and was the capital of the Ait Ba’arame tribe famous for its resistance against the Spanish.

before.title: Sidi Ifni – Tafraoute
body: From Sidi Ifni we turn north again back to Tiznit, where we stop to wander the soukhs. From here we enter the Anti Atlas mountains, passing Tighmi and the Kerdous pass, then Tizourhane until we reach Tafraoute. This road is one of the most beautiful roads in the Moroccan mountains.

before.title: Tafraoute – Taroudant
body: After breakfast we visit the famous painted rocks, colored in 1984 by the Belgian artist, Jean Verame. He used 18 tons of blue, pink, red, and black paint, helped in his project by men from the Tafraoute fire-brigade. This work of art has proved very controversial; people choosing to wonder at it, question its existence and to despise it. It is certainly an individual and “other” piece of art. We then set out northwards continuing to follow the spectacular road which the Ait Baha river to the town of the same name. Later we turn right towards Taroudant, “the little Marrakesh”, so called for the similarity of its ramparts and town walls to those of the “red city”. Here we spend the night having explored the town.

before.title: Tafraoute – Chagaga
body: After breakfast we continue towards the desert. We cross the two passes of Tizi-n-Tighatine and Tizi-n-Ikhsane before reaching Kourkouda and Taznakht . This small town is famous for its Berber kelims and carpets, lunch in Foum-Zguid. From here we continue south and drive into the Sahara across the stony desert, “reg” and across the now dried-up Lake Iriqui. In the middle of this lake we can search for fossils. And arriv Chagaga dunes here you take a camel ride and can clamber up to the top of the high dunes to watch the sunset. At the foot of the dunes, we have dinner and spend the night in a camp of nomad tents.

before.title: Chagaga – Ouarzazate
body: After breakfast in the desert camp, the itinerary crosses another 60 km of desert road via the Sacred Oasis to arrive in M’hamid You continue to north up the Draa Valley towards Zagora for lunch. This small town is the largest oasis in the Draa Valley and is particularly famous for its dates. From here we follow the ancient caravan route used by the caravans that had crossed the Sahara for days and weeks bringing treasures from Mali or Mauretania. The road passes between the river and the mountains past all the Kasbahs and the local gardens giving you a clearer impression of life here in this area of Morocco. In Agdez at the head of the Draa Valley, you can stop to visit the oldest and most famous kasbah in the valley, Kasbah Tamnougalte. It is still partly inhabited by about eleven families. You then continue to Ouarzazate crossing the Tizi-n-Tififte pass, where some scenes from the film “Babel” were shot. In Ouarzazate you stay in Hotel/Riad.

before.title: Ouarzazate – Marrakesh
body: After breakfast, driving north from Ouarzazate, you leave the main road and take a side road to Ait ben Haddou, which also belonged to the Lords of the Atlas, the Glaoui family. This is the most famous Kasbah in Morocco and a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is also well-known as being the backdrop to many Hollywood blockbusters, such as “Alexander”, “the Gladiator”, “the Kingdom of Heaven” The road then continues along the Ounila valley with beautiful and prosperous villages, stunning mountains and views to Telouet, where you will stop to visit the Kasbah and perhaps have lunch. We reach Marrakesh by the early evening.

body: Leaving Essaouira after breakfast, you follow the coastal road south with constant views of the Atlantic, often battering the rocks and sending up picturesque spray as it beats against the rocks. We pass Agadir and continue south to Tiznit, the town famous for its silver jewelry. From here we turn towards the sea and take the particularly beautiful coastal road to Sidi Ifni. This is a little neat blue and white town with a distinctly Spanish feel to it. It takes its name from a local holy man and was the capital of the Ait Ba’arame tribe famous for its resistance against the Spanish.

after.title: Sidi Ifni – Tafraoute
body: From Sidi Ifni we turn north again back to Tiznit, where we stop to wander the soukhs. From here we enter the Anti Atlas mountains, passing Tighmi and the Kerdous pass, then Tizourhane until we reach Tafraoute. This road is one of the most beautiful roads in the Moroccan mountains.

after.title: Tafraoute – Taroudant
body: After breakfast we visit the famous painted rocks, colored in 1984 by the Belgian artist, Jean Verame. He used 18 tons of blue, pink, red, and black paint, helped in his project by men from the Tafraoute fire-brigade. This work of art has proved very controversial; people choosing to wonder at it, question its existence and to despise it. It is certainly an individual and “other” piece of art. We then set out northwards continuing to follow the spectacular road which the Ait Baha river to the town of the same name. Later we turn right towards Taroudant, “the little Marrakesh”, so called for the similarity of its ramparts and town walls to those of the “red city”. Here we spend the night having explored the town.

after.title: Taroudant – Chegaga
body: After breakfast we continue towards the desert. We cross the two passes of Tizi-n-Tighatine and Tizi-n-Ikhsane before reaching Kourkouda and Taznakht . This small town is famous for its Berber kelims and carpets, lunch in Foum-Zguid. From here we continue south and drive into the Sahara across the stony desert, “reg” and across the now dried-up Lake Iriqui. In the middle of this lake we can search for fossils. Arrive at the Chegaga dunes, where you take a camel ride and can clamber up to the top of the high dunes to watch the sunset. At the foot of the dunes, we have dinner and spend the night in a camp of nomad tents.

after.title: Chagaga – Ouarzazate
body: After breakfast in the desert camp, the itinerary crosses another 60 km of desert road via the Sacred Oasis to arrive in M’hamid You continue to north up the Draa Valley towards Zagora for lunch. This small town is the largest oasis in the Draa Valley and is particularly famous for its dates. From here we follow the ancient caravan route used by the caravans that had crossed the Sahara for days and weeks bringing treasures from Mali or Mauretania. The road passes between the river and the mountains past all the Kasbahs and the local gardens giving you a clearer impression of life here in this area of Morocco. In Agdez at the head of the Draa Valley, you can stop to visit the oldest and most famous kasbah in the valley, Kasbah Tamnougalte. It is still partly inhabited by about eleven families. You then continue to Ouarzazate crossing the Tizi-n-Tififte pass, where some scenes from the film “Babel” were shot. In Ouarzazate you stay in Hotel/Riad.

after.title: Ouarzazate – Marrakesh
body: After breakfast, driving north from Ouarzazate, you leave the main road and take a side road to Ait ben Haddou, which also belonged to the Lords of the Atlas, the Glaoui family. This is the most famous Kasbah in Morocco and a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is also well-known as being the backdrop to many Hollywood blockbusters, such as “Alexander”, “the Gladiator”, “the Kingdom of Heaven” The road then continues along the Ounila valley with beautiful and prosperous villages, stunning mountains and views to Telouet, where you will stop to visit the Kasbah and perhaps have lunch. We reach Marrakesh by the early evening.

after.title: Free Day
body: Free Day to explore Marrakech Red City with a guided tour!

after.title: Explore the Atlas Mountains
body: This morning from Marrakech, your Mountain guide and private vehicle will meet you at the hotel/riad at 09:00 in the morning to start the journey for 1h30, and then Your hike will first go up to the Tirst Plateau and down to Ouirgane forest, full of junipers and pine trees. Then, it is on to the Tasa Ouirgane with a small village. Here, we will have lunch in a local Berber family’s home and finally head back a different route to the Marirgha and travel back to Marrakech. The total walking time will be five hrs.

body: Transfer to Marrakech airport, and then fly home with plenty of fun!!

body: Transport , Breakfast, English speaking Local Guide

Explore the cultural and spiritual center of Morocco during this full day tour of Fes. Also known as Fes el Bali, this UNESCO World Heritage Site was founded in the 9th century, and is home to the world’s oldest university. The city of Fes reached its true economic and cultural height in the 13th–14th centuries under the Merinids, when it replaced Marrakech as the capital of the kingdom. Although the political capital of Morocco was transferred to Rabat in 1912, Fes has retained its status as the country’s Artisan centre. Artisan workshops in the medina are as active today as they were 100 years ago, and strongly contribute to the city’s industrial economy. Trades such as blacksmithing, leather working, ceramics, silk, tapestries, and sculpting are still practiced in these workshops today. The original ramparts still protect this ancient city and its estimated 9000 narrow passageways and bustling streets.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

before.title: Fes – Erfoud – Merzouga
body: Transport (7hrs), Breakfast, Dinner, Driving distance: 480km

If you’re up to it you can also ride a camel!

before.title: Ouarzazate – Ait Ben Hadou – Tichka Pass – Marrakech
body: Transport (4hrs), Breakfast, Dinner, Driving distance: 200km

Located approximately 30 kilometers from Ouarzazate this fortified village (or ksar) is ideally positioned along a once frequented, ancient caravan route linking the Sahara and Marrakech. Ait Ben Haddou has been used in numerous Hollywood film productions for its distinctive architecture. In 1987 this famed location was deemed a UNESCO World Heritage Site. An evocative relic of the time when the Glaoui clan ruled over the Atlas and Marrakech, the palace was the family’s Headquarters and was situated in a dramatic location, on a broad mountain valley, providing sweeping views of the peaks on all sides. Continue from here back onto the main road back to Marrakech, crossing on the dramatic Tizi n’Tichka passage through the High Atlas Mountains range on the way. Whilst passing take time to notice the many beautifully-terraced valleys and adobe villages perched precipitously on the hillsides, Arrive to Marrakech in the late aftrnoon.

before.title: Marrakech Guided Visit
body: Transport, Local English speaking guide, Breakfast

This morning around 9am your English speaking City tour guide will be meet you at your hotel/riad. And start your tour usually starts at the 12th century Koutoubia Mosque. This mosque’s beautiful minaret dominates the skyline of Marrakech and can be seen from almost every approach to the city thanks to a long-standing planning ordinance that forbids any other building in the old city to rise above the height of a palm tree. You will also visit the El-Bahia Palace, this 19th century palace is elaborate in its decoration and was built over a period of seven years for Ba Ahmed, the son of the Grand Vizier Si Moussa. There are row after row of apartments—that once housed Ahmed’s harem—a trapezoidal garden, a huge tiled courtyard, and many hidden treasures, both in the form of antique objects d’art and the palace’s convergence of Andalusian and Moorish architecture. One of most visited sites in Morocco is the Saadian Tombs which were only accessible via the mosque next door. However, in 1917 they were opened to the public and can now be accessed via a narrow passage that leads to an enclosed garden watched over by two mausoleums that include more than one hundred mosaic decorated tombs. The Koranic School Medersa Ben Youssef which is a Theological college founded by the Merenid Sultan Abu Hassan in the 14th century, and restored in 1564 by the Saadians who made it the largest theological college in the Maghreb and a rival to the important Medersa Bou Inania in Fés. Your tour lasts from 9:30am until 05:00pm

body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 180km

You will dive into its history and see how as an original Phoenician trading post, it prospered during the Roman era as citizens extracted the Tyrian purple colour from a local shellfish. Explore the fortifications that ring the city were built by the Portuguese and is inherent to the charm of Essaouira. You will have time to see the other attractions including the port, where a daily supply of fresh fish can be found, and the tremendous beach that stretches away to the south. The easy-going nature of the town, the medina, the dramatic fortifications and the beach, have created a bohemian atmosphere quite different from the rest of the country. At the end of the tour you will be transferred to your hotel in Essaouira.

An evocative relic of the time when the Glaoui clan ruled over the Atlas and Marrakech, the palace was the family’s Headquarters and was situated in a dramatic location, on a broad mountain valley, providing sweeping views of the peaks on all sides. Continue from here back onto the main road back to Marrakech, crossing on the dramatic Tizi n’Tichka passage through the High Atlas Mountains range on the way. Whilst passing take time to notice the many beautifully-terraced valleys and adobe villages perched precipitously on the hillsides, Arrive to Marrakech in the late afternoon.

after.title: Marrakech Guided Visit
body: Transport, Local English speaking guide, Breakfast

This morning around 9am your English speaking City tour guide will be meet you at your hotel/riad. And start your tour usually starts at the 12th century Koutoubia Mosque. This mosque’s beautiful minaret dominates the skyline of Marrakech and can be seen from almost every approach to the city thanks to a long-standing planning ordinance that forbids any other building in the old city to rise above the height of a palm tree. You will also visit the El-Bahia Palace, this 19th century palace is elaborate in its decoration and was built over a period of seven years for Ba Ahmed, the son of the Grand Vizier Si Moussa. There are row after row of apartments—that once housed Ahmed’s harem—a trapezoidal garden, a huge tiled courtyard, and many hidden treasures, both in the form of antique objects d’art and the palace’s convergence of Andalusian and Moorish architecture. One of most visited sites in Morocco is the Saadian Tombs which were only accessible via the mosque next door. However, in 1917 they were opened to the public and can now be accessed via a narrow passage that leads to an enclosed garden watched over by two mausoleums that include more than one hundred mosaic decorated tombs. The Koranic School Medersa Ben Youssef which is a Theological college founded by the Merenid Sultan Abu Hassan in the 14th century, and restored in 1564 by the Saadians who made it the largest theological college in the Maghreb and a rival to the important Medersa Bou Inania in Fés. Your tour lasts from 9:30am until 05:00pm
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

after.title: Marrakech – Atlas Mountain
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast, Lunch at Berber Family House or Picnic,Driving distance: 120km

After breakfast around 9am, your driver will be picked you up, And head south to the atlas Mountains, Youll meet your English speaking Mountain guide at the starting point of your option hike, Atlas Mountains Ouirgane (Wirgane) offers a great variety of optional activities. Choose between mountain biking, hiking, horseback and Mule riding, This morning from Marrakech, your guide and private vehicle will meet you at the hotel/riad at 09:00 in the morning to start the journey for 1h30, and then Your hike will first go up to the Tirst Plateau and down to Ouirgane forest, full of junipers and pine trees. Following, you will continue to L’khmis Village, the village of Torourd , and then up through the Azaden Valley with very nice views of Takhrkhourt (large forest) in Toubkal National Park . Then, it is on to the Tasa Ouirgane with a small village. Here, we will have lunch in a local Berber family’s home and finally head back a different route to the Marigha and travel back to Marrakech. The hiking time will be flexible to you in between 1 – 5hrs hike.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

after.title: Marrakech – Essaouira
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 180km

From Marrakech towards the coast Atlantic Essaouira. The approximate travel time is 3 hours. Enjoy a private tour of Essaouira, one of the most picturesque towns in the country. You will dive into its history and see how as an original Phoenician trading post, it prospered during the Roman era as citizens extracted the Tyrian purple colour from a local shellfish. Explore the fortifications that ring the city were built by the Portuguese and is inherent to the charm of Essaouira. You will have time to see the other attractions including the port, where a daily supply of fresh fish can be found, and the tremendous beach that stretches away to the south. The easy-going nature of the town, the medina, the dramatic fortifications and the beach, have created a bohemian atmosphere quite different from the rest of the country. At the end of the tour you will be transferred to your hotel in Essaouira.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

after.title: Free Day in Essaouira
body: Transport, Breakfast

body: Airport Transport, Breakfast

before.title: Fes Guided Visit
body: Explore the spiritual and cultural heart of Morocco!

- The Royal Palace (Dar el Makhzen): Admire the majestic golden gates surrounded by intricate zellij tilework.
- Mellah (Jewish Quarter): Discover the history of the Jewish community and see the 17th-century Ibn Danan Synagogue.
- Bou Inania Madrasa: A masterpiece of Marinid architecture, famous for its detailed wood carvings and stucco.
- Tanneries of Chouara: Watch traditional leather-making methods from a rooftop terrace overlooking the colorful dye pits — a must-see sight!
- Al-Qarawiyyin University and Mosque: Founded in 859 AD, this is the oldest continually operating university in the world.
- Souks and Artisan Quarters: Explore workshops where artisans craft copperware, ceramics, textiles, and jewelry using age-old techniques.
- Borj Nord Viewpoint: For a panoramic view of Fes Medina and its surrounding hills — perfect for photos!
Lunch Suggestion:
Enjoy a traditional Moroccan meal in a local riad restaurant — try dishes like chicken tagine with preserved lemons, or couscous with caramelized onions and raisins.
Afternoon Options (Optional Add-ons):
- Visit the Dar Batha Museum, showcasing Moroccan arts and crafts.
- Explore the modern city of Fes el-Jdid for a contrast between old and new.
Overnight in Fes at a traditional riad within the medina.

before.title: Fes → Ifrane → Midelt → Erfoud → Merzouga (Desert Gate)
body: After an early breakfast, depart Fes around 7:00 AM for a scenic journey toward the Sahara Desert. Travel through the ever-changing landscapes of the Middle Atlas Mountains, passing through charming towns, lush valleys, and dramatic plateaus.
Highlights along the way:
- Ifrane – “The Little Switzerland of Morocco”
A charming alpine-style town known for its clean streets, flower gardens, and European architecture.
- Azrou Cedar Forest
Stop to see the famous Barbary macaque monkeys in the cedar forest — a fun moment for nature and wildlife lovers.
- Middle Atlas & Ziz Valley
Continue past Midelt, nestled between the Middle and High Atlas, and descend through the Ziz Gorge, a dramatic canyon leading to the fertile Ziz Valley, lined with date palms and ancient kasbahs.
- Erfoud & Merzouga Dunes
As you reach the edge of the desert, the scenery transforms into golden sands and vast open plains — your first glimpse of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga.
Arrive in Merzouga by late afternoon, where your camel caravan awaits. Ride across the dunes at sunset to reach your luxury desert camp, nestled among the towering sands.
Evening Experience:
Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a starlit sky, followed by live drumming and storytelling around the campfire — an unforgettable night in the Sahara.

before.title: Merzouga Desert → Todra Gorge → Dades Valley
before.accommodation: Boutique Kasbah or Guesthouse in Dades or Skoura
body: Wake up early to witness one of Morocco’s most unforgettable sights — the sunrise over the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi. The first rays of light paint the sand in glowing shades of amber and gold, offering the perfect photo moment.

After breakfast, enjoy a camel trek back across the dunes, Continue your journey north through Erfoud, famous for its date market and fossil workshops, then pass through Tinejdad, where you can visit the Berber Museum of Culture to gain insight into local traditions and desert heritage.

Soon, you’ll arrive at the majestic Todra Gorge (Tinghir region) — a natural wonder carved by the Todra River through towering limestone cliffs that rise up to 300 meters high. Enjoy time to walk along the gorge floor, where locals tend small gardens and rock climbers challenge the sheer canyon walls.

After lunch at the gorge, the route winds west toward the Dades Valley, often called the “Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs.” Here, the scenery transforms into spectacular red and ochre rock formations, including the famous “Monkey Fingers” cliffs and dramatic switchback roads leading up the valley.
Arrive by late afternoon and settle into a cozy guesthouse or kasbah-style hotel surrounded by palm groves and ancient fortified villages.
Evening Experience:
Relax on the terrace with panoramic views of the Dades Gorge, enjoy a homemade dinner, and experience the warm Berber hospitality of the valley.

before.title: Dades Valley → Ouarzazate → Aït Ben Haddou → Imlil (High Atlas)
body: After breakfast, depart from the Dades Valley and follow the scenic road toward Kelaat M’Gouna, also known as the Valley of Roses . This charming area is famous for its spring rose festival and for producing delicate rosewater and essential oils. You may stop at a local cooperative to see how these traditional products are made by Berber women using time-honored techniques.

Continue your drive through the Skoura Oasis , a lush valley of palm groves and ancient kasbahs (fortified homes), including the well-preserved Kasbah Amridil, one of the most beautiful and iconic kasbahs in southern Morocco. The landscapes gradually change from fertile valley floors to the arid, cinematic plains surrounding Ouarzazate , often called the “Hollywood of Africa.”

Here, you can visit the world-famous Atlas Film Studios, where international movies and series like Gladiator, The Mummy, and Game of Thrones were filmed. A guided visit reveals the impressive sets, props, and stories behind Morocco’s thriving film industry.

Just a short drive further west brings you to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aït Ben Haddou , a striking example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture. This ancient ksar (fortified village), perched on a hill along the old caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakech, has been featured in numerous films and remains one of Morocco’s most photogenic sites. Stroll through its narrow alleys and climb to the top for breathtaking panoramic views over the desert plain and the snow-capped Atlas Mountains.

After lunch overlooking the kasbah, the journey continues over the dramatic Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m) , the highest road pass in Morocco. Enjoy sweeping views of mountain valleys, Berber hamlets clinging to terraced slopes, and the ever-changing colors of the High Atlas.

By late afternoon, descend into the serene Imlil Valley , nestled at the foot of Mount Toubkal (4,167 m) — North Africa’s highest peak. The air becomes cooler and fresher as you reach this charming mountain village, surrounded by walnut groves, terraced fields, and traditional stone houses.
Evening Experience:
Settle into a cozy riad or mountain lodge. Enjoy a home-cooked Berber dinner and the tranquil ambiance of the High Atlas, where the only sounds are the river and distant mule bells.

before.title: Imlil: Berber Villages Hike & Traditional Lunch
body: Wake up to the fresh mountain air and the sound of birds echoing across the valley. After breakfast at your riad, set off on a gentle hike through the scenic Imlil Valley (1,740 m) — the gateway to Mount Toubkal. Your local mountain guide will lead you along ancient mule trails that connect the Berber villages scattered across the slopes of the High Atlas.

The walk passes through terraced fields, apple and walnut groves, and crystal-clear mountain streams, where villagers still draw water using traditional irrigation channels. Along the way, you’ll visit picturesque hamlets such as Aroumd, Tamatert, or Armed, where stone-built houses blend naturally into the surrounding mountainsides.

Enjoy frequent stops for photos and for meeting friendly locals going about their daily lives — women baking bread in clay ovens, children playing by the water channels, and farmers tending to their mules or small orchards.

Around midday, you’ll be warmly welcomed into a Berber family home for a freshly prepared traditional lunch — often featuring tajine, homemade bread, olive oil, and mint tea. It’s a wonderful opportunity to experience authentic mountain hospitality and learn about Berber customs, traditions, and daily routines in this remote yet welcoming region.

After lunch, enjoy a leisurely walk back down to your riad or guesthouse, where the rest of the afternoon is free to relax — perhaps on the terrace overlooking the snow-capped peaks or with a cup of Moroccan tea as the sun sets over the valley.
Evening Experience:
Enjoy a cozy dinner prepared with local ingredients and spend a peaceful night under the stars of the High Atlas.

before.title: Imlil → Marrakech
body: After breakfast, say goodbye to the peaceful mountains and the friendly faces of Imlil as you begin your journey back to the vibrant city of Marrakech. The drive winds gently down through the Aït Mizane Valley, offering spectacular views of terraced fields, walnut trees, and snow-capped peaks in the distance.

Pass through Asni, a lively market town where locals from nearby villages gather to trade fresh produce, livestock, and handmade goods. If it’s a Saturday, you may even catch the weekly souk — a colorful scene filled with the aromas of spices, fresh mint, and grilled corn.

Continue descending into the Haouz Plain, where the landscape gradually shifts from rugged mountain terrain to open farmland dotted with olive groves and adobe villages. As the red walls of Marrakech come into view, you’ll feel the contrast between the calm of the High Atlas and the bustling rhythm of the “Red City.”

Upon arrival in Marrakech, check into your riad or hotel, ideally located within or near the Medina — the city’s historic heart. The rest of the day is yours to relax or begin exploring the city’s rich heritage:
- Enjoy a rooftop dinner overlooking Jemaa el-Fna Square, where storytellers, musicians, and food stalls bring the night to life.
Evening Suggestion:
Treat yourself to a traditional hammam (Moroccan spa) or a dinner show with live music and belly dancing for a memorable evening back in the city.

before.title: Marrakech Guided Visit
body: Start your day with a guided exploration of Marrakech, Morocco’s most captivating imperial city — a perfect blend of history, culture, and vibrant energy.

Begin at the Majorelle Garden, an oasis of exotic plants and cobalt-blue art once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Continue to the Koutoubia Mosque, Marrakech’s iconic landmark, and the Bahia Palace, a masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture filled with intricate mosaics and carved ceilings.

Stroll through the narrow lanes of the Medina, a UNESCO World Heritage site, where you’ll discover colorful souks brimming with spices, textiles, lanterns, and leather goods. Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa, an ancient Islamic school famed for its stunning craftsmanship (optional visit depending on time).

In the afternoon, experience the magic of Jemaa el-Fna Square, the beating heart of Marrakech. Here, snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls bring the square to life as the sun sets over the city.
Overnight in Marrakech.

before.title: Departure from Marrakech or Casablanca
body: After breakfast, enjoy some free time to relax or explore Marrakech at your own pace — perhaps do some last-minute shopping in the souks or unwind at a traditional hammam.
At the scheduled time, your driver will transfer you to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.
If your flight departs from Casablanca, you’ll travel via the highway (approx. 2.5–3 hrs drive).
Your unforgettable 12-day Moroccan adventure comes to an end — filled with the colors, flavors, and warm hospitality of Morocco.
Thank you for traveling with Toubkal Peaks Travel!

after.title: Departure from Marrakech or Casablanca
body: After breakfast, enjoy some free time to relax or explore Marrakech at your own pace — perhaps do some last-minute shopping in the souks or unwind at a traditional hammam.
At the scheduled time, your driver will transfer you to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.
If your flight departs from Casablanca, you’ll travel via the highway (approx. 2.5–3 hrs drive).
Your unforgettable 12-day Moroccan adventure comes to an end — filled with the colors, flavors, and warm hospitality of Morocco.
Thank you for traveling with Toubkal Peaks Travel!

before.title: Marrakech → Ait Ben Haddou (≈180 km / 4 hrs)
body: Your journey begins with a morning pick-up from your hotel or riad in Marrakech. From the vibrant streets of the city, you will ascend into the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m), Morocco’s highest mountain road. Along the way, the scenery unfolds with terraced valleys, snow-capped peaks in winter, and small Berber villages clinging to the mountainsides.

Your first stop is Kasbah Telouet, an ancient palace of the powerful Glaoui family. Wander through the crumbling walls and beautifully carved doors while imagining the lives of Morocco’s historic elites. Continue to the UNESCO-listed Ait Ben Haddou, an iconic hilltop kasbah made of red clay, famously featured in films like Gladiator and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the winding streets, climb to the panoramic viewpoints, and capture unforgettable photographs of the kasbah with the surrounding valley bathed in the afternoon light.
Spend the night in a traditional Moroccan-style hotel nearby, enjoying local cuisine and the calm of the Atlas foothills.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

before.title: Ait Ben Haddou → Dades Valley (≈160 km / 3.5 hrs)
body: After breakfast, depart from Ait Ben Haddou and continue eastwards, crossing the rugged Sarhro Mountains. The landscape changes dramatically from the lush High Atlas to jagged volcanic peaks and deep gorges. You’ll notice the contrast of rocky terrain punctuated by abandoned kasbahs, silent witnesses to Morocco’s rich history.

As you approach the Draa Valley, Morocco’s longest river valley, the scenery softens into fertile green stretches dotted with palm groves, mud-brick villages, and traditional irrigation systems known as khettaras. Stop along the way to explore Berber villages, meet local families, and experience a glimpse of everyday life in rural Morocco. The valley offers incredible photography opportunities, especially at sunset when the golden light illuminates the palm groves and kasbahs.
Arrive in Zagora for an overnight stay, your gateway to the Sahara Desert.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

before.title: Dades Valley → Todra Gorge → Nekob → Zagora (≈250 km / 5 hrs)
body: This morning begins with a visit to Todra Gorge, one of Morocco’s most impressive natural formations. Towering sandstone cliffs rise nearly 300 meters above the valley floor, creating narrow canyon paths ideal for short walks and photography.

Continue towards Nekob, a traditional Berber town with ancient kasbahs, local markets, and mud-brick architecture. Stroll through the town, interact with locals, and witness traditional crafts being made.

The drive back through the Draa Valley offers additional scenic viewpoints of palm groves, kasbahs, and small villages tucked along the valley floor. Each stop presents a perfect chance to photograph the contrast of desert landscapes against green oases. Arrive in Zagora in the late afternoon, where you can relax and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of this desert gateway.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

before.title: Zagora → M’Hamid → Erg Chigaga (≈160 km / 5 hrs)
body: Today’s journey takes you deeper into the edge of the Sahara Desert. Begin with a stop at Tamgrout (Tamegroute), a village renowned for its green pottery. Witness Berber artisans creating distinctive green-glazed bowls, pots, and decorative items using traditional techniques. Don’t miss the 13th-century Koran library, an underground repository of ancient manuscripts, showcasing centuries of Moroccan Islamic scholarship.
Continue to M’Hamid, the last town before the expansive desert. Explore the palm groves and mud-brick houses while enjoying lunch and a taste of local life.
From M’Hamid, your 4×4 will traverse the wild desert landscapes, with occasional stops at small oases such as Oasis Sacré, a hidden water source amidst the arid plains.

Arrive at Erg Chigaga, where the vast golden dunes await. Enjoy a camel trek at sunset (~45 minutes) across the shifting sands, capturing the breathtaking colors of the desert as the sun dips below the horizon. Afterward, settle at your desert camp, experiencing traditional Berber hospitality and a night under the stars.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

before.title: Erg Chigaga → Marrakech (≈421 km / 9 hrs)
body: Rise early to witness a desert sunrise, with the soft morning light transforming the dunes into golden waves. After breakfast, begin the return journey to Marrakech by 4×4, crossing the Paris-Dakar route, famous for its challenging sand dunes and rocky desert tracks.
Stop at Taznakht, a village renowned for its handmade Berber carpets. Watch weavers at work and shop for unique souvenirs.

As you ascend the High Atlas Mountains once again, enjoy panoramic views of rugged peaks and valleys before descending into Marrakech. Arrive in the city in the evening, completing a journey that spans mountains, valleys, and the vast Sahara Desert.
Meals: Breakfast

body: After breakfast, leave Ait Ben Haddou and drive east to Ouarzazate, the “Hollywood of Africa”, then on through the Skoura palm oasis, dotted with old kasbahs such as Kasbah Amridil.

Continue along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs to Kelaat M’Gouna, the Valley of Roses, where local cooperatives make rosewater and rose oils. Stop in Berber villages along the way, with the High Atlas to the north and the Saghro mountains to the south.
Arrive in the Dades Valley in the afternoon and settle in among its red cliffs and unusual rock formations, perfect for photos in the late light.

before.title: Arrival in Marrakech – Gateway to the High Atlas
body: Welcome to Morocco! Upon arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport, you’ll be met by our driver and transferred to your charming riad in the old medina. The rest of the day is free to stroll through the maze-like souks, admire the colorful spice stalls, and soak in the energy of Jemaa el-Fna square, where storytellers, snake charmers, and food vendors come alive at sunset. This first evening is all about relaxation and preparing yourself for the mountain adventure ahead.
- Overnight in Marrakech

before.title: Marrakech – Imlil – Trek to Toubkal Refuge (3,207m)
body: After breakfast, we leave the bustle of Marrakech behind and drive into the High Atlas Mountains (1h30). At Imlil village (1,740m), we meet our local muleteers who will carry luggage, leaving us free to ascend with skis and light packs.

The skinning begins gently through Berber villages and terraced fields, before entering the wilder Mizane Valley. A stop at the Chamharouch shrine (2,310m)—a spiritual site visited by pilgrims—offers a cultural glimpse. From here, the path climbs steadily, snow becoming deeper as we approach the alpine world. By afternoon we reach the Toubkal Refuge (3,207m), nestled beneath steep cliffs. Here, hot tea and a warm dinner await.
- 5–6 hrs trek / +1,467m ascent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

before.title: Ski Ascent of Mount Toubkal (4,167m)
body: Today we tackle North Africa’s highest peak. An early start allows us to skin up the south cwm, zig-zagging through snowy slopes. The climb is steady but demanding at altitude.

Reaching the summit cross of Toubkal (4,167m) is a thrilling moment—panoramic views stretch across the entire Atlas chain, with the Sahara Desert shimmering to the south. After a well-earned rest, comes the highlight: a long ski descent back to the refuge, weaving turns down wide open slopes.
- 6–7 hrs / +960m ascent / –960m descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

before.title: Ski Ascent of Ras & Timesguida Ouanoukrim (4,083m & 4,089m)
body: We venture west towards the Ouanoukrim massif, home to the second- and third-highest peaks in North Africa. Using skins and sometimes crampons for steeper sections, we climb towards Ras (4,083m) and Timesguida (4,089m).
The ridge here offers dramatic alpine scenery, with jagged peaks and plunging valleys. From the summits, the reward is an exhilarating ski descent back to the refuge, carving turns in the fresh snow.
- 6 hrs / +900m ascent / –900m descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

before.title: Ski Ascent of Akioud (4,030m)
body: Today’s target is Akioud Peak, a quieter but equally rewarding summit. The climb takes us through remote slopes, sometimes narrow couloirs, before opening onto wide, ski-friendly terrain.
The descent is a highlight of the trip, combining technical sections with sweeping runs. Back at the refuge, the group can relax over mint tea and hearty mountain food.
- 5–6 hrs / +820m ascent / –820m descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

before.title: Tizi n’Ouanoums (3,670m) & Secret Valleys
body: This day is reserved for exploration. We skin up to the Tizi n’Ouanoums Pass (3,670m), a natural gateway into hidden valleys of the High Atlas. Depending on snow and weather, we may ski technical couloirs or explore untouched bowls.
It’s a day of discovery, often with few other skiers in sight—just the silence of the mountains and the crunch of skis on snow.
- 5 hrs / +500–700m ascent & descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

before.title: Final Descent – Refuge to Imlil – Marrakech
body: After days of high peaks, it’s time for one last descent. From the refuge, we enjoy a long ski run down to Imlil, passing once again through alpine valleys and Berber hamlets.
At Imlil, we say goodbye to our mule team and transfer back to Marrakech (1h30). The afternoon is free for hammam baths, souvenir shopping, or a celebratory dinner overlooking the bustling square.
- 4–5 hrs descent
- Overnight in Marrakech

body: Depending on flight times, enjoy a relaxed morning in Marrakech before your airport transfer. End of services and farewell to Morocco.

before.title: Arrival in Casablanca – Rabat
body: Depending on your time of arrival, you might like to see some of the sights of Casablanca, in particular the Hassan II Mosque with the tallest minaret in the world. Casablanca (Spanish for “White House” and generally abbreviated by locals as “Casa”) has long stood in the western imagination as a hub of romance. Most travelers associate Casablanca with tales of the Marrakesh Express and, of course, the film, Casablanca. Of course, the reality of this fast-paced Moroccan city is quite different , you’ll visit the Hassan II Mosque it’s The largest mosque Morocco (and the 13th largest in the world) with the tallest minaret in the world. It was completed in 1993 and stands on the Northern Atlantic coast of Morocco, looking back over the Casablanca city line. Designed by Michel Pinseau and built by the Bourges, the minaret is 210 meters high and has a laser at the top which is directed towards Mecca. and then contunie your journey to Rabat , overnight at the Hotel/Riad .

before.title: Rabat – Essaouira
body: Airport Transfer (5hrs 30minutes)
This morning after your breakfast you’ll visit of Rabat,

What is the capital of Morocco? Many people believe it’s Casablanca but in fact Rabat is the capital. In 1912 with the beginning of the French protectorate of Morocco the capital was moved from Fez to Rabat. In 1956 when independence was regained it was decided that the capital would stay put. Rabat isn’t on the tourist radar but there are many reasons to include it on your list. When it comes to seeing Morocco, Rabat is a bit of an unsung hero. The administrative capital is often left off the popular tourist circuit and folks tend to flock to Marrakech in the south and Fes, as well as Tangier and Chefchaouen in the central and northern parts of the country. Even Casablanca likely gets more traction than Rabat as it’s the location of the busiest international airport in Morocco as well as the largest mosque in North Africa, Hassan II , Kasbah Odayas ; Chellah Garden ; and then heading to Essaouira. The costal road offres beautiful scenery, an area famous for the Argan trees. Here you will see herds of goats climbing the Argan trees looking for better food than they can find on the ground. After several stops along the coast we get to Essaouira in the afternoon, Overnight accommodation at a riad in the Medina.

before.title: Free Day to Explore Essaouirra ( Today you don’t need a guide its very samall and easy city to discover on your one ).
body: Transport, Breakfast

Breakfast at the hotel in Essaouira, then start your explorative journey of the city. You’ll visit the Skala Fortress; see Thuya wood carved by artisans; walk through the alleys of the medina and view hundreds of handicrafts. Today your driver can help you to have lunch in a Moroccan way, freshly bought fishes ‘cooked to order’. In the afternoon, you will have some free time to wander around , go to the beach and enjoy time to yourselves. Essaouira is also referred to as The “City of the Wind” and it attracts surfers from all over the world. Essaouira knew many civilizations – including the Portuguese occupation, which affects much of its architecture – however, it remains a small village with much history. Because of its size and its characteristic blue doors and washed walls, it is also regarded as Morocco’s “Jewel of the Atlantic”. There is an annual festival of “Gnawa music”, where many musical groups come from different parts of Africa and the world. Usually it starts in the second week of June. Overnight accommodation.

before.title: Essaouirra – Marrakech
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast

After breakfast in your riad, you will have some free time before leaving for Marrakech. On our way – since this is the land of Argan culture – this is an opportunity to visit the women’s co-operative of Argan oil where they extract the oil that is famous for its culinary, cosmetic and medical properties. After several stops to take photographs, you will continue your travel to Marrakech and check in to your riad. After dinner you will have the option to enjoy walking within the famous square of Jemaa El fna, entertained with magicians, story tellers, musicians and snake charmers

before.title: Marrakech Guided Tour
body: Private Guided Visit, Breakfast

This is your discovery day in the Red City, aided by your private guide who will meet with you in the morning at your riad to discuss the day’s possibilities. Leave the everyday behind as you dive into the souks, the markets that have provided Marrakschis with all their needs for over one thousand years. Vibrant colors, rich aromas, cat-calls and music, merchants in djellabas, street chefs in white hats, whatever your image of the exotic is you will find it in Marrakech. A visit to the Museum of Photography or the Majorelle Gardens are also highly recommended, visit the Souk, la Bahia Palace. Ali ben Youssef medersa (koranic school) & Musee de Marrakech to see the atrium), secret garden You can read more about our thoughts on the Red City in our Marrakesh travel guide Book that will give you a good understanding of what there is to see and do. The tour lasts from 9:30am until 5:30pm

before.title: Marrakech – Atlas Mountains – Marrakech
body: Transport (2hrs), Breakfast, Lunch

This relaxed day trip will take you from the walls of the ‘Red City’ to the High Atlas hamlet of Ouirgane. En route you’ll make a stop at the busy little town of Asni which is a buzz of activity as local Berbers ply to sell their produce, particularly on Saturdays – market day. Once in Ouirgane your time is free to explore the village. Fed by the Oued Nfis from the Atlas, a perennial water source, the village is surprisingly verdant – a real oasis in the mountains. In recent years a dam was built creating a reservoir which adds to the visual appeal of the valley. Market day is Thursday in Ouirgane.

The most popular activity for visitors is walking – several circuits offer options for people of all abilities, from an hour’s stroll along village tracks, past typical Berber houses, farms and fields, to more challenging walks through the valley and along the river. Your guide will brief you on options when you arrive. Alternatively, enjoy the fresh mountain air and views from a cafe. Lunch is taken in a typical Berber village house, enjoying a home-cooked meal. After lunch you have time to discover more of the picturesque Ouirgane Valley, the timing its flexible from 1 to 4hrs, after the hike youll take a 1Hr journey back by car to Marrakech , overnight at the same riad .

body: Transport (3hrs to casablanca), (25min to Marrakech airport ), Breakfast, ( Marrakech to Casablanca Distance Km 223 ).
Your Morocco adventure will be coming to an end today. Do plan on having a full three hours at the airport today since customs can be slow. We truly hope you enjoyed your journey with our team!

body: Private Guided Visit, Breakfast

This is your discovery day in the Red City, aided by your private guide who will meet with you in the morning at your riad to discuss the day’s possibilities. Leave the everyday behind as you dive into the souks, the markets that have provided Marrakchis with all their needs for over one thousand years. Vibrant colors, rich aromas, cat-calls and music, merchants in djellabas, street chefs in white hats, whatever your image of the exotic is you will find it in Marrakech. A visit to the Museum of Photography or the Majorelle Gardens are also highly recommended, visit the Souk, la Bahia Palace. Ali ben Youssef medersa (koranic school) & Musee de Marrakech to see the atrium), secret garden You can read more about our thoughts on the Red City in our Marrakesh travel guide Book that will give you a good understanding of what there is to see and do. The tour lasts from 9:30am until 5:30pm

after.title: Marrakech – Atlas Mountains – Marrakech
body: Transport (2hrs), Breakfast, Lunch

This relaxed day trip will take you from the walls of the ‘Red City’ to the High Atlas hamlet of Ouirgane. En route you’ll make a stop at the busy little town of Asni which is a buzz of activity as local Berbers ply to sell their produce, particularly on Saturdays – market day. Once in Ouirgane your time is free to explore the village. Fed by the Oued Nfis from the Atlas, a perennial water source, the village is surprisingly verdant – a real oasis in the mountains. In recent years a dam was built creating a reservoir which adds to the visual appeal of the valley. Market day is Thursday in Ouirgane.

The most popular activity for visitors is walking – several circuits offer options for people of all abilities, from an hour’s stroll along village tracks, past typical Berber houses, farms and fields, to more challenging walks through the valley and along the river. Your guide will brief you on options when you arrive. Alternatively, enjoy the fresh mountain air and views from a cafe. Lunch is taken in a typical Berber village house, enjoying a home-cooked meal. After lunch you have time to discover more of the picturesque Ouirgane Valley, the timing its flexible from 1 to 4hrs, after the hike youll take a 1Hr journey back by car to Marrakech , overnight at the same riad .

before.title: Fez Guided Visit

before.title: Fez – Ziz Valley – Merzouga
body: Transport (7hrs) , Breakfast , Dinner

before.title: Merzouga – Gnaoua Music – Camel Ride , Desert Camp
body: Transport (1hr), Breakfast , Dinner

After breakfast in the hotel you’ll start your explorative desert journey of the area, visiting the village of Khamlia, originally slaves from Sudan to experience their music and lifestyle. Not far away there’s the lake of Merzouga, with its bird populations, including flamingos. You may also like to visit the nomad wire house where many Berber handicrafts are priced lower than in the big cities. On the afternoon you will ride camel, guided by an experienced Camel man, to explore inside the mysterious sand-sea of the Erg-Chebbi. Here you’ll spend your first night under the stars, or if you prefer, in a traditional Berber nomad tent. Dinner will be served in the tent where you will spend the night. Dinner Bed and Breakfast.

before.title: Desert Camp – Todra Gorge – Ouarzazate or Ait Ben Haddou
body: Transport (6hrs), Breakfast , Dinner

After breakfast in the hotel we’ll drive through the Dades Valley towards Kalaa M’gouna and Ouarzazat. The route through Dades Valley is the way of the thousand kasbahs – providing numerous opportunities to take some of your best photographic shots of the trip. We’ll stop at Kalaa Mgouna, “the rose city”, to purchase the rosewater, which will make your linen smell good a long time after your trip is over. Continue to Skoura and the dirds valley; visit the Kasbah Ameridil, a well-preserved kasbah in this area. After lunch, you will have some time for hiking within the valley and then continue to Ouarzazate – “the Hollywood of Africa”- whose geography and beautiful landscapes have attracted many world class movie producers, Overnight accommodation will be in riad.

before.title: Ouarzazate – Taznakhte – Taroudant
body: Transport (4hrs), Breakfast

After breakfast in your riad, we’ll head to Taroudant via Taznakht, visiting Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah, the largest Kasbah in Morocco. Built during the beginning of the XXth Century by T-hami El Glaoui -one of the last Berber chieftains -Ben Haddou Kasbah used to be one of his stops during his long travel from the sub-Saharan countries to Marrakech, and is now a UNESCO world heritage site. On to Taliouine, the capital of saffron in Morocco, you have the option to visit the Safran co-operative. If your visit coincides with the saffron harvest, you will have the opportunity to meet the Berber people with their families harvesting the saffron in their fields. We should arrive at Taroudant in the afternoon, here you will see the ramparts and walk within the small alleys in the Medina. Taroudant is always referred to as “The little Marrakech” because it was the built by the Saadian dynasty who used it as their capital before they moved to Marrakech in the 16th century.

before.title: Taroudant – Agadir – Essaouira
body: Transport (4h30m), Breakfast

Breakfast in the riad, and then head for Essaouira, travelling via Agadir. Our first stop will be at Agadir, a resort city which was a very big tourist destination for many years. After lunch and a small walk along the Promenade, you will continue to Essaouira. The coastal road offers beautiful scenery, an area famous for the Argan trees. Here you will see herds of goats climbing the Argan trees looking for better food than they can find on the ground. After several stops along the coast we get to Essaouira in the afternoon. Overnight accommodation at a riad in the Medina.

before.title: Free day in Essaouira
body: Breakfast at the hotel in Essaouira, then start our explorative journey of the city. You’ll visit the Skala Fortress; see Thuya wood carved by artisans; walk through the alleys of the medina and view hundreds of handicrafts. Today you will have lunch in a Moroccan way, freshly bought fishes ‘cooked to order’. In the afternoon, you will have some free time to wander around , go to the beach and enjoy time to yourselves. Essaouira is also referred to as The “City of the Wind” and it attracts surfers from all over the world. Essaouira knew many civilisations – including the Portuguese occupation, which affects much of its architecture – however, it remains a small village with much history. Because of its size and its characteristic blue doors and washed walls, it is also regarded as Morocco’s “Jewel of the Atlantic”. There is an annual festival of “Gnawa music”, where many musical groups come from different parts of Africa and the world. Usually it starts in the second week of June.

The sightseeing tour will cover several impressive sights: The Koutoubia mosque, Majorelle Gardens, Bahia Palace and Dar Si Said Palace museum of jewellery. Optional lunch will be in the medina followed by a walk through the colorful souks of Marrakech. Enjoy a sunset drink overlooking the exciting Jamaa El Fna Square from a terrace of a cafe, dinner and night at hotel.
